author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's stored date and description are offered for change and validated as at booking. A successful correction replaces that visit's details in place and shows the owner's record; a refused one offers the details again.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction of a booked visit offers that visit's stored date and description for change.
Submitting a description and a date later than today leaves that visit carrying the submitted details and shows the owner's record.
A pet with one booked visit still has exactly one visit after a correction of it succeeds.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the details are offered again.
A date of today or earlier is refused and the date is named.
An owner's record offers no way to correct a visit.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit, or removing one (NG-5, NG-4).
Any link, button, or other way in to correction from the owner's record or any other page. Correction is reachable only by addressing the visit directly.
Changing which pet or owner a visit belongs to.
Recording who corrected a visit, or what it said before.
notes: Non-goal ADR authored for the narrowing: docs/adr/2026-08-11-non-goal-visit-correction.md (product-requirements-expert write scope). Two follow-ups belong to system-design-expert, which owns those paths: (1) add the index row for it to docs/adr/README.md; (2) annotate docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md as superseded in part for its NG-5 half. Two open questions recorded in the PRD, deliberately unanswered here: behavior when a correction names a visit that is not the named pet's, and whether a way in follows. Take the narrowest reading of each if implementation forces the issue.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: NG-5 is narrowed. Cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope; correcting its date and description is now in scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction extends the existing visit-booking path rather than adding one. It stays in the owner feature package on VisitController, entered through the Owner aggregate root exactly as booking is (system-design.md#contracts, 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'). No new module, pattern, dependency, or trust boundary. The one adjustment is an extension point: the controller's @ModelAttribute loader gains a branch on an optional visitId, and Pet gains an identity lookup for its visits mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). Route: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. Basis for the covering claim is grep plus direct file reads of VisitController, Owner, Pet, Visit, and the template (IDE oracle not connected in this run) - the weaker basis, but each cited symbol was read in full.
integration_points: Bind: keep the model attribute name 'visit'. VisitController.loadPetWithVisit already supplies it and runs before every handler in the class, so the correction handlers reuse it unchanged. Give it @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId. When null, keep today's behavior exactly (new Visit(), pet.addVisit(visit)). When present, return the stored visit and do NOT call pet.addVisit - Spring then binds the submitted date and description onto the stored instance in place.

Load: owners.findById(ownerId) -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisit(visitId). Add Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id): iterate the visits, skip new ones, match on id, return null when absent. Prefer that over a stream filter in the controller so the null-on-absent convention lives in one place, next to the existing Owner.getPet.

Persist: mutate the stored Visit in place, then this.owners.save(owner). Owner->Pet->Visit is @OneToMany(cascade = ALL), so the save issues an UPDATE against the existing visit row. The visit keeps its identity, and the pet's visit count is unchanged by construction rather than by an explicit check - that is what satisfies 'no additional visit'.

Validate: @Valid Visit gives the blank-description rejection from Visit's @NotBlank. Repeat the non-future date rule with the identical rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate") call the booking path uses; extract it to one private method both handlers call so the two paths cannot drift. On result.hasErrors() return "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm" and do not save.
Redirect: "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}" on success, as booking does.

Template: no change is required. createOrUpdateVisitForm.html already branches on ${visit['new']} for its heading, and its form carries no th:action, so it posts back to whatever URL rendered it. The file target is satisfied by reuse.

patterns.description: the @ModelAttribute("visit") loader that resolves owner and pet from the path before every handler - the branch point for correction
Owner.getPet(Integer id) - the identity-lookup shape Pet.getVisit(Integer id) should mirror, including null on absent
the codebase's existing create-or-update-on-one-controller precedent, including the isNew() branch
the non-future date rule to share verbatim between booking and correction

risks.risk: The loader runs before EVERY handler in VisitController. Left unbranched, a correction request would construct a new Visit and attach it to the pet, so the GET would show tomorrow's date and the POST would save a second visit - failing three acceptance criteria at once.
risks.mitigation: Branch on the optional visitId inside the loader, and cover it with theCorrectedPetShouldGainNoAdditionalVisit asserting the fixture pet's visit count after the POST.

risks.risk: Identity tampering through the form: a submitted id field could repoint the correction at another pet's visit.
risks.mitigation: The existing @InitBinder already disallows "id" and "*.id". Keep it. Identity comes from the path alone, and the path is resolved through the owner-pet-visit chain, so a visit outside the named pet is unreachable.

risks.risk: A new success message would be a new user-facing English string, and REQ-LANG-002 requires every user-facing key to exist in all eleven bundles under messages/.
risks.mitigation: Add no flash message and no new message key. Redirecting to the owner's record satisfies 'shows the owner's record' on its own. Leave the submit button's #{addVisit} label alone for the same reason.

risks.risk: Correction is a mutating POST reachable by any caller.
risks.mitigation: No new exposure: NG-1 declines access control project-wide, and the 'Unauthenticated data modification' row of system-design.md#threat-model already covers the owner, pet, and visit mutation routes. No new trust boundary is introduced, so none needs placing.

notes: OPEN QUESTION 1 - a correction naming a visit that is not the named pet's. Narrowest reading: Pet.getVisit returns null, and the controller throws IllegalArgumentException with the same message shape the loader already uses for a missing owner or pet. No new error-handling pattern, no new route, no silent creation, no cross-pet edit. OPEN QUESTION 2 - a visible way in. Narrowest reading: none. Do not touch ownerDetails.html; its visits table keeps only the existing 'Add Visit' link. The acceptance criterion 'An owner's record offers no way to correct a visit' is the assertion for this, and the 2026-08-11 ADR names the absence a scope boundary. TESTING - VisitControllerTests is @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean OwnerRepository. Its @BeforeEach fixture Owner is the same instance the loader mutates, so the visit-count assertion is observable directly on the fixture pet after the POST; the fixture needs a Visit with an id set, since Pet.getVisit must skip new visits. AGGREGATE NOTE - Visit inherits no equals or hashCode override from BaseEntity, so mutating a Visit already inside Pet's LinkedHashSet is safe, and @OrderBy("date ASC") is a load-time ordering only. ROUTE NOTE - /visits/new and /visits/{visitId}/edit differ in segment count, so no mapping ambiguity arises. DURABLE MEMORY WRITTEN THIS DISPATCH - (1) docs/adr/README.md: index row added for 2026-08-11-non-goal-visit-correction.md, and the 2026-08-08 row's status now records the partial supersession; (2) docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md: Status line and a dated annotation under Decision record that the NG-5 half is superseded in part and the immutability clause no longer holds whole, with NG-4 unchanged; (3) docs/system-design.md: VisitController and Visit contract rows now cover correction and cite REQ-VIS-003, and the aggregate-invariant paragraph records that a stored visit is reached by identity through its pet. AUTOFIX AUDIT - no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theVisitCorrectionFormShouldOfferTheStoredDateAndDescription asserts the prefilled visit via two separate MockMvc andExpect(model().attribute("visit", hasProperty(...))) Hamcrest checks. Every other assertion in this same file that inspects a Visit's fields (theCorrectedVisitShouldCarryTheSubmittedDetails) does so with chained AssertJ assertThat(...).isEqualTo(...) on the domain object directly, per testing-principles.md's AssertJ Assertions checklist ('Chained assertions on same object preferred over separate assertThat() calls'). The two styles for the same category of check, in the same file, are inconsistent and the Hamcrest form is redundant when MockMvc's MvcResult already exposes the bound model object.
findings.fix: Capture the MvcResult from mockMvc.perform(...).andReturn(), pull the "visit" model attribute, and assert it with one chained AssertJ call: assertThat(visit.getDate()).isEqualTo(BOOKED_VISIT_DATE); assertThat(visit.getDescription()).isEqualTo(BOOKED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION); (or a single .satisfies / .extracting chain), matching the style used two tests later in the same file.

findings.description: VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET names and claims to exercise 'a visit that is not the named pet's' (matching the acceptance criterion and the design's cross-pet-mismatch decision), but the @BeforeEach fixture constructs only one pet with one visit (id 2). The constant 99 is never attached to any second pet or second visit in the test's arrange phase - it is simply an id absent from the sole pet's visit set. The test therefore only proves 'an unrecognized visitId is refused,' which happens to also cover the cross-pet case only because Pet.getVisit's null-on-absent behavior treats both the same way. The test name and constant overclaim the scenario it actually arranges, and a future reader relying on this test as a specification for cross-pet isolation would be misled if the lookup implementation ever changed to search across pets.
findings.fix: Either (a) rename the test and constant to reflect what is actually arranged (e.g. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIdIsUnrecognized / UNRECOGNIZED_VISIT_ID), or (b) arrange a second pet with its own visit and use that visit's real id as VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET, so the test demonstrates cross-pet isolation rather than mere non-existence.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Identity is taken exclusively from the path and resolved through the owner->pet->visit chain: owners.findById(ownerId) throws on absence, Owner.getPet(petId) iterates only that owner's pets, and the new Pet.getVisit(visitId) iterates only that pet's visits and returns null otherwise. Verified independently of the implementer's claim: no request can reach a visit belonging to another pet or owner; a foreign visitId fails closed with IllegalArgumentException (VisitController.java:71-90, Pet.java:91-101).

Repointing is not reachable. Visit carries no association field (no pet/owner reference; the pet_id column is owned by Pet's unidirectional @OneToMany @JoinColumn), so no submitted parameter can move a visit between pets. The pre-existing @InitBinder disallowing 'id' and '*.id' is unchanged and still covers both bound model attributes (visit and owner), so identifier tampering via form binding stays blocked - the mitigation the system-design threat model records for mass assignment holds for the new endpoint.

Correction mutates the stored instance in place and persists through the owner aggregate (owners.save(owner)); no second visit is created and no orphan is written. spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (application.properties:11), so the refusal paths cannot leak a mutated-but-invalid visit to the database via dirty checking outside an explicit save.

Validation parity with booking: @Valid on Visit keeps @NotBlank on description, and rejectDateNotInFuture applies the same non-future-date rule to correction as to booking. No validation was weakened on the new path.

No injection surface added. Both identifiers are typed (int/Integer), so a non-numeric segment fails binding rather than reaching persistence; data access remains Spring Data JPA derived queries with no string-concatenated SQL. The redirect target 'redirect:/owners/{ownerId}' resolves from the typed path variable, so it is not attacker-steerable (no open redirect).

Output escaping unchanged: no template was modified, the correction reuses pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, and user-derived visit fields are rendered through Thymeleaf's escaping th:field/th:text bindings. A grep for th:utext across src/main/resources/templates returns nothing. The thrown error messages echo only the caller's own integer identifiers, so they leak no other record's data.

Supply chain unchanged: the change set touches no build.gradle, settings.gradle, or gradle/ file, so no dependency was added, upgraded, or repointed and no new CVE surface enters with this change. No credential, token, or key literal appears anywhere in the diff (docs and Java sources only).

Newly exposed attack surface is one more unauthenticated mutating route, which is the already-recorded posture of this application (system-design.md Security Context and Threat Model: no authentication, authorization, or CSRF anywhere, every route open). The handler binds the Owner model attribute exactly as the pre-existing booking handler does, so it grants no capability an unauthenticated caller lacks today via /owners/{ownerId}/edit. This is the documented pre-existing condition, not a regression introduced here.

Validate: @Valid Visit gives the blank-description rejection from Visit's @NotBlank. Repeat the non-future date rule with the identical rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate") call the booking path uses; extract it to one private method both handlers call so the two paths cannot drift. On result.hasErrors() return "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm" and do not save.
Redirect: "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}" on success, as booking does.

Template: no change is required. createOrUpdateVisitForm.html already branches on ${visit['new']} for its heading, and its form carries no th:action, so it posts back to whatever URL rendered it. The file target is satisfied by reuse.
Document: the loader's three-step identity resolution and its IllegalArgumentException on an unresolvable step are recorded in system-design.md#contracts under 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'.

risks.risk: The loader runs before EVERY handler in VisitController. Left unbranched, a correction request would construct a new Visit and attach it to the pet, so the GET would show tomorrow's date and the POST would save a second visit - failing three acceptance criteria at once.

risks.risk: Identity tampering through the form: a submitted id field could repoint the correction at another pet's visit.
risks.mitigation: The existing @InitBinder already disallows "id" and "*.id". Keep it. Identity comes from the path alone, resolved through the owner-pet-visit chain, and a step that does not resolve throws - so a visit outside the named pet is unreachable. Now stated in system-design.md so a reader learns it is deliberate.

risks.risk: A new success message would be a new user-facing English string, and REQ-LANG-002 requires every user-facing key to exist in all eleven bundles under messages/.
risks.mitigation: Add no flash message and no new message key. Redirecting to the owner's record satisfies 'shows the owner's record' on its own. Leave the submit button's #{addVisit} label alone for the same reason.

risks.risk: Correction is a mutating POST reachable by any caller.
risks.mitigation: No new exposure: NG-1 declines access control project-wide, and the 'Unauthenticated data modification' row of system-design.md#threat-model already covers the owner, pet, and visit mutation routes. No new trust boundary is introduced, so none needs placing.

title: Correcting a visit that is not the named pet's is refused

acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction of a booked visit offers that visit's stored date and description for change.
Submitting a description and a date later than today leaves that visit carrying the submitted details and shows the owner's record.
A pet with one booked visit still has exactly one visit after a correction of it succeeds.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the details are offered again.
A date of today or earlier is refused and the date is named.
A correction naming a visit that the named pet does not hold is refused, whether it is opened or submitted.
An owner's record offers no way to correct a visit.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit, or removing one (NG-5, NG-4).
Any link, button, or other way in to correction from the owner's record or any other page.
Changing which pet or owner a visit belongs to.
Presenting the mismatch refusal differently from how booking's equivalent mismatch is presented.

author: change-grader
summary: add visit correction endpoints to VisitController

blast_radius.note: Eight files in one package plus its docs, two modules, no sensitive paths; the only shared-path edit is loadPetWithVisit, which is purely additive because a null visitId reproduces the previous booking behavior verbatim and the existing booking tests still pass.

semantic_surprise.note: processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and calls owners.save(owner), so Spring binds every request parameter onto the whole owner aggregate before it is persisted: a POST to the correction URL carrying firstName, address, telephone or even pets[0].name is bound and saved, since @InitBinder disallows only id and *.id rather than allow-listing date and description. The shape is inherited verbatim from processNewVisitForm, so it is a replicated surface rather than a new class of flaw, but the correction endpoint doubles it and the diff reads as if only a visit's date and description are writable. Secondary: the shared future-date rule means a visit whose date has already passed can never be corrected even to fix its description alone, and the reused createOrUpdateVisitForm template still submits under the addVisit label and lists the visit being corrected under Previous Visits.

test_adequacy.note: Six new tests assert real outcomes rather than restating the implementation: the stored visit's mutated date and description, containsExactly on pet.getVisits() to pin that no second visit is added, the typeMismatch.visitDate error code on the boundary, and both the GET and POST arms of the cross-pet refusal against a genuine sibling pet holding a real visit. Only the seventh PRD criterion, that no page links to correction, rests on a grep rather than an assertion, and the mocked repository leaves the save call itself unverified.

reviewer_hedging.note: All three reviewers the risk-proportional fix-delta plan dispatched approved with empty findings lists, and the round-one findings were all fixable autofix or clarify items that the recorded approvals name as resolved; security-reviewer sits outside this round's roster with an earlier approval on src that has not moved, which is expected rather than silence.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries and zero consultations; the single design revision is a re-triage that verified the revised criteria were already satisfied and changed no code. The NG-5 narrowing in prd.md and the two ADR edits are the explicit reopening path the 2026-08-08 ADR itself set, and the deliberate absence of a link into the feature is stated as a scope boundary rather than an omission.

rationale: Correct against the requirement and cleanly reviewed, but the correction handler binds request parameters onto the entire Owner aggregate and saves it, so a submit can rewrite owner fields. Inherited from the booking handler, not introduced. Read that handler and decide whether to allow-list the binder now.
